items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: when I came to Paris with Dizzy and I stayed over and he asked me to play with him... we found that we had been kids together.

ctx.x: Oh, well, it doesn't matter. I just thought I'd ask.
But he had an orchestra at the time, and when I came to Paris with Dizzy and I stayed over and he

asked me to play with him. Now, we didn't recognize each other that time, because this was like '40, almost 30 years. So we began talking one day and he said, 'Little Kenny. Pittsburgh.' He said, 'I know a little Kenny from Pittsburgh, used to go to Washington School.' I said, 'Well, that's me.' He said, 'It can't be true.' And we found that we had been kids together.

items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: But you were working out the rhythm end of it. That's right, and it seemed to all fit in together.

ctx.x: Well, I guess that for Diz and Bird were -- had their thing, and working it out, you know, from the melodic point of view. The rhythmic and melodic combined. But you were working out the rhythm end of it.
That's right, and it seemed to all fit in together.
